description: Inspect a 200A residential service entrance panel for code violations including workmanship, terminations, working space clearances, overcurrent protection, and panel configuration.
environmentDescription: A residential garage with a 200A service entrance panel, exposed conductors, breakers, main disconnect, and surrounding working space.

violations.description: Unsecured conductors in panel with poor workmanship

citations.text: Install electrical equipment tidily, with good workmanship.

violations.hintText: Look at how the wires are arranged inside the panel. Are they neat and properly secured?
violations.inspectionNote: Conductors inside the panel are loose and crossing over each other. NEC requires neat and workmanlike installation.

violations.description: Aluminum service entrance conductor terminated on copper-only rated lug

citations.text: Terminations must make a solid connection without damaging the conductor, and connectors and terminals must be rated for the conductor's material.

violations.hintText: Check the main lugs. Is the conductor material compatible with the lug rating? Look for AL/CU markings.
violations.inspectionNote: Aluminum conductor is terminated on a lug rated for copper only. This can cause overheating due to dissimilar metal expansion rates.

violations.description: Working space in front of panel is less than 36 inches deep

citations.text: Working space in front of live parts must be at least as deep as Table 110.26(A)(1) requires; for 0 to 150 V nominal that is 3 feet.
Keep at least 1 m of clear working space about electrical equipment wherever it must be reached for operation or maintenance.
citations.description: Working space in front of panel is less than 1 m deep
citations.hintText: Measure the clear space in front of the panel. Is there at least 1 m of unobstructed working space?
citations.inspectionNote: Storage boxes are stacked within 24 inches (about 610 mm) of the panel face. The code calls for at least 1 m of working space.

violations.hintText: Measure the clear space in front of the panel. Is there at least 36 inches of unobstructed working space?
violations.inspectionNote: Storage boxes are stacked within 24 inches of the panel face. NEC requires a minimum 36-inch clear working space.

sceneFact.note: Clear depth in front of the panel face

violations.description: Service disconnect located in an area not readily accessible

citations.text: Put the service disconnect where it is readily accessible, outside the building or inside near where the service conductors enter.

violations.hintText: The service disconnect must be readily accessible. Can you reach it without moving obstacles or using a ladder?
violations.inspectionNote: Service disconnect is located behind stored equipment and requires moving obstacles to access. Must be readily accessible per NEC.

violations.description: 12 AWG conductor protected by a 30-ampere overcurrent device

citations.text: Protect conductors (except flexible cords) from overcurrent according to their ampacity.
A device protecting copper conductors from 14 AWG to 10 AWG is limited to 15 A for 14 AWG, 20 A for 12 AWG and 30 A for 10 AWG, and generally cannot be rated above the conductor's ampacity.

violations.hintText: Verify that each conductor's ampacity matches or exceeds its breaker rating. 12 AWG is rated for 20A max.
violations.inspectionNote: A 12 AWG conductor (rated 20A) is connected to a 30A breaker. The conductor could overheat before the breaker trips.

violations.description: Breaker operating handle center is mounted above 6 feet 7 inches

citations.text: Keep breakers and switches within easy reach: with the handle raised to its top position, the middle of its grip must be no higher than 6 ft 7 in. (2.0 m) off the floor or working platform.

violations.hintText: Check the height of the topmost breaker handle. The center of the grip must not exceed 6 feet 7 inches.
violations.inspectionNote: The top breaker's operating handle center is at approximately 7 feet. This exceeds the NEC maximum of 6 ft 7 in.

violations.description: Panel circuit directory is missing or has inaccurate circuit descriptions

citations.text: Label every circuit, and every change to a circuit, clearly with its specific purpose, in enough detail to tell it apart from all others.

violations.hintText: Examine the circuit directory inside the panel door. Is every circuit clearly and accurately labeled?
violations.inspectionNote: Several circuits are labeled generically as 'spare' or 'misc' while actively serving loads. The 2026 NEC requires specific, clear identification.

violations.description: More circuit breakers installed than the panel's rated number of spaces

citations.text: A panelboard must physically prevent installing more overcurrent devices than the number it was designed, rated and listed for.

violations.hintText: Count the breakers and compare with the panel's rated space count. Are tandem breakers used in non-approved locations?
violations.inspectionNote: Tandem breakers are installed in slots not designed for them, exceeding the panel's rated number of circuits. This overloads the bus bars.
